title: NBA Offseason Daily Digest
subtitle: September 25, 2026: Training Camps Approach Amidst Blockbuster Moves

items.headline: NBA Legend Bob Pettit Dies at 93
items.summary: Basketball Hall of Famer and the NBA's first-ever MVP, Bob Pettit, has passed away at the age of 93. Pettit, an 11-time All-Star, led the St. Louis Hawks to the 1958 NBA championship and was the first player to reach 20,000 career points.

items.headline: LeBron James Joins 76ers in Blockbuster Offseason Move
items.summary: Four-time MVP LeBron James has signed with the Philadelphia 76ers, ending his tenure with the Lakers. He will team up with newly acquired Jaylen Brown in what is considered one of the most significant free-agency signings of the offseason.

items.headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo Traded to Miami Heat
items.summary: In another shocking offseason move, two-time MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo was traded from the Milwaukee Bucks to the Miami Heat in June, dramatically reshaping the Eastern Conference landscape.

items.headline: Kawhi Leonard Agrees to 2-Year, $115M Extension with Raptors
items.summary: Kawhi Leonard and the Toronto Raptors have reportedly agreed to a two-year, $115 million extension. This deal solidifies Leonard's future with the team ahead of training camp.

items.headline: Thunder GM Presti Discusses Roster Changes After Key Trades
items.summary: Oklahoma City Thunder GM Sam Presti acknowledged the team's 'different makeup' for the upcoming season after trading longtime starter Lu Dort and key reserves to shed salary. The Thunder, coming off a 64-win season, will feature new roles for players like Jared McCain, Ajay Mitchell, and Cason Wallace.

items.headline: Jaylen Brown Heads to 76ers, Paul George to Celtics in Big Swap
items.summary: Jaylen Brown was traded from the Boston Celtics to the Philadelphia 76ers in exchange for Paul George and draft picks, forming a new 'Big Three' in Philadelphia alongside LeBron James and Joel Embiid.

items.headline: Pelicans Acquire AJ Johnson, Taj Gibson, Extend Saddiq Bey
items.summary: The New Orleans Pelicans had a quiet draft, opting out of first-round picks for 2026, but were active in trades and extensions. They acquired AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson from the Grizzlies and signed Saddiq Bey to a three-year, $55.5 million veteran contract extension.

items.headline: Clippers Waive Johni Broome Amidst Roster Reshaping
items.summary: The Los Angeles Clippers waived Johni Broome, ending his short stint ahead of the 2026-27 season. The Clippers have been busy reshaping their roster, adding Rui Hachimura and Max Strus in separate moves.

items.headline: Jalen Duren's Contract Standoff with Pistons Continues
items.summary: All-Star center Jalen Duren remains a restricted free agent, reportedly considering a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer after rejecting a five-year, $200 million proposal from the Detroit Pistons. The deadline for Duren to accept the qualifying offer is October 1.

items.headline: Marcus Smart Departs Lakers for Rockets, Citing 'Disrespectful' Offer
items.summary: Veteran guard Marcus Smart signed a two-year, $12.4 million deal with the Houston Rockets, leaving the Los Angeles Lakers. Smart stated that the Lakers' offer was 'disrespectful' given his performance.

items.headline: Pelicans Bolster Roster with Mathurin, Re-sign DeAndre Jordan
items.summary: The New Orleans Pelicans made key free agent signings, including Bennedict Mathurin on a two-year, $15.375 million deal, and re-signed DeAndre Jordan to a two-year minimum contract.

items.headline: NBA Training Camps Set to Open Next Week, Preseason Soon After
items.summary: The NBA offseason is nearing its end as training camps for the 2026-27 season are scheduled to open on September 29. Preseason games will then tip off on October 3.

items.headline: 2026-27 NBA Regular Season Schedule Unveiled
items.summary: The NBA released its full 82-game schedule for the 2026-27 season in August. Opening night on October 20 features a tripleheader, including Boston at Detroit, Philadelphia at New York, and Oklahoma City at San Antonio.

items.headline: Lakers GM Rob Pelinka Sets Expectations for Post-LeBron Era
items.summary: With LeBron James' departure, Lakers GM Rob Pelinka has set high expectations for the team, emphasizing a playoff run every year. Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves are poised to lead the franchise into this new era.
